extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computer algebra system (mathematicians, computational algebraists, and advanced users needing ring/field functionality)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for using the Magma system: controlling the user environment (editing, interrupts, timing, scrolling, memory limits) and creating/operating on rings and fields (constructors, element creation, tests, and category-dependent operations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor invocation for line editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the line editor for the current line, or the editor specified by the EDITOR environment variable (or /bin/ed if unset). Example: %e84 edits line 84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typing %e<linenumber> opens that line in the preferred editor; after saving and exiting the editor, the changed line is used. Use EDITOR environment variable to select a different editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrupting a computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Press control-c once to request an interrupt; Magma will interrupt as soon as possible. Press control-c twice quickly (within half a second) to force a stop that exits the entire Magma system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a single control-c to stop a long-running calculation so you can try an alternative approach. Use double control-c only as a last resort because it exits the whole session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing Magma operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure CPU time of statements using the time prefix or the Cputime/Cputime(t) functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefix a statement with time to print CPU seconds for that statement (note: CPU time ≠ wall-clock time). To time several statements collectively, do t := Cputime(); ...; print Cputime(t);. Cputime() with no arguments returns time since session start; with an argument returns time since that argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrolling output
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SetRows(n) to limit output to n rows at a time and prompt the user to continue; SetRows(0) disables the filter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When output exceeds n rows, Magma pauses after each block of n rows and prompts (e.g., 'Press return for more:'). Useful when the host system cannot scroll output back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory limit (soft limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set a soft memory allocation limit for Magma via SetMemoryLimit(n) or the MAGMA_MEMORY_LIMIT environment variable; GetMemoryLimit() returns the current soft limit (0 = no soft limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a soft limit to avoid excessive swapping on shared systems for large tasks. The OS still imposes a hard cap independent of this soft limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserved words
rubrics_metrics.description: List of language reserved words (e.g., do, elif, else, end, procedure, intrinsic, function, for, if, while, etc.) that have special syntactic meaning in Magma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use reserved words as identifiers. The manual provides a complete reserved word list to consult when naming variables and functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator precedence and associativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma defines a precedence table and associativity rules for operators (groups from highest to lowest precedence, with specified left/right/non-associative behavior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the precedence table when writing expressions to understand binding (e.g., unary -, ^, *, +, comparisons, logical operators, etc.). Use parentheses to disambiguate complex expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of the grammar (program, statement, expression forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma's syntax is described in grammar form: program → statement | directive | intrinsic, with detailed productions for directives, statements (including time prefix, lval list := expr ;, if/then/else, loops, print, function/procedure definitions), expressions, literals and constructors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the grammar for writing syntactically correct Magma programs; the manual enumerates forms for directives, statements, expressions, constructors (map, rec, str, seq, set, etc.), and index/list/range notations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating rings and fields — standard creation functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many rings/fields can be created directly with intrinsic functions: IntegerRing (ZZ), RationalField (Q), RealField (IR), ComplexField (C), FiniteField (GFq), ResidueClassRing(ZZ/mZZ), PolynomialRing, PowerSeriesRing, NumberField, pAdicField, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate intrinsic with required arguments (some require none). Examples: Q := RationalField(); Z12 := ResidueClassRing(12); G := FiniteField(5,2). Some constructors accept multiple argument forms (e.g., FiniteField(25) ≡ FiniteField(5,2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recursive ring constructions and caution on approximate ground rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Rings can be constructed recursively from coefficient/ground rings (e.g., polynomial rings over a field); beware that using approximate ground rings (like real/complex) can lead to numerical instabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building rings recursively (e.g., polynomial or algebra constructors over IR or C), be mindful that approximate arithmetic may cause unexpected behavior—prefer exact base rings when exactness is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring constructors: sub, ideal, quo, ext, comp, loc
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructors create new rings from existing ones: sub< R | gens > returns a subring and embedding; ideal< R | gens > creates an ideal; quo< R | I > creates a quotient ring and map; ext< R | f > creates algebraic extensions; comp< F | gens > completes a field; loc< R | gens > localizes at an ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructors often return two values: the new object and the natural embedding/mapping. Not all constructors apply to all categories. Examples: sub< G | g^26 > returns subring and embedding; quo< R | f > returns quotient and natural map. Use appropriate constructors for the category and be aware of returned category differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: ext constructor: polynomial and algebraic extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: ext< R | > is equivalent to PolynomialRing(R) (univariate); ext< R, n | > is PolynomialRing(R,n) (multivariate). The algebraic extension ext< F | f > creates an extension by a root of a monic irreducible polynomial f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ext< F | f > after verifying IsIrreducible(f) to construct algebraic field extensions. For transcendental extensions, ext< R | > produces polynomial rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: comp constructor / Completion
rubrics_metrics.description: comp< F | list of ideal generators > (or Completion(F,I)) returns the completion of F at ideal I and a map from F to the completion. Examples include LaurentSeriesRing(Q) and pAdicField(3) equivalences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comp when you need completions; examples: comp< F | 0 > may equal LaurentSeriesRing(Q), comp< Q | 3 > equals pAdicField(3). Ensure the ideal is appropriate (zero or prime ideal of ring of integers).

rubrics_metrics.name: loc constructor / Localization
rubrics_metrics.description: loc< R | list of ideal generators > (or Localization(R, P)) returns the localization of R at a prime ideal P and a mapping from R to the localization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use loc when working with valuation/local rings (example: localization of ZZ at 5 yields valuation ring of Q_5). The function returns both the localized ring and the embedding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residue class fields vs quotient rings; FieldOfFractions and IntegerRing
rubrics_metrics.description: quo< R | I > yields a quotient ring (may be in a non-field category); to obtain a residue class field in a field category use ResidueClassField(R, I) or quo< Cat : R | I > with an explicit field category. FieldOfFractions(D) constructs the field of fractions of an integral domain; IntegerRing(K) returns ring of integers of a field K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about desired category when creating fields. Example: quo< FldNum : R | x^2+7 > returns a number field, whereas quo< R | x^2+7 > returns a quotient polynomial algebra. Use ResidueClassField for residue class fields and FieldOfFractions(IntegerRing()) for Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element creation and coercion into a ring
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of a ring R can be created by coercion (R ! value), by expression in generators, or by special constructors. Representative(R) / Rep(R) returns a representative element; Random(R) yields a random element of finite rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Z12 := Integers(12); Z12 ! 57 yields 9. For polynomial rings: p := R ! [coeffs]. Use Random(R) only for finite rings and Representative(R) when needed to inspect canonical representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming generators and accessing generators (angle brackets, AssignNames, R.i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Angle brackets in a construction R<names> both set the printed names for indeterminates and assign identifiers in the session. AssignNames(~R, names) changes printed names; R.i accesses the i-th generator independent of local identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using R<s,t> assigns s and t as both printed names and session identifiers. Reassigning those identifiers later does not change the ring's printed form. Use R.1, R.2 to access generators if angle-bracket identifiers were not used or were reassigned. AssignNames allows changing printed names later; length of name list ≤ number of generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero(R) and One(R) and creating identities via coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: Zero(R) returns the additive identity and One(R) the multiplicative identity of ring R; coercion of integers 0 and 1 also yields these identities. Exact division operator div returns results in the ring when division is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: M := MatrixRing(Integers(12),3); One(M) and M ! 0 produce identity and zero matrices. Use div for exact division within a ring (6 div 3 yields an Integer Ring element). Use / to produce elements possibly in a field of fractions (6/3 → Rational Field).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring element arithmetic operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard arithmetic available: +, -, *, unary -, ^, inverse, / (division by unit), div (exact division), and exponentiation with integer exponents. There are also specialized operators (&+, &*, &and, &or, &meet, ... ) used in particular contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of units when using /; ^ with negative exponent requires unit. Use provided specialized operators for algebraic constructions as documented in operator tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests on elements of rings (IsZero, IsOne, IsUnit, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean predicates test element properties: IsZero(x), IsOne(x), IsMinusOne(x), IsUnit(x), IsNilpotent(x) (returns index if true), IsZeroDivisor(x), IsRegular(x), IsIdempotent(x), IsIrreducible(x), IsPrime(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these Is* functions to query algebraic properties of elements. Some predicates return supplementary information (e.g., nilpotence index). Availability depends on implemented algorithms for the category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests on ring properties (IsField, IsOrdered, IsEuclideanDomain, IsPID, IsUFD, IsDomain, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean functions test algebraic properties of rings: IsField(R), IsOrdered(R), IsEuclideanDomain(R), IsEuclideanRing(R), IsPrincipalIdealDomain(R)/IsPID, IsPrincipalIdealRing(R)/IsPIR, IsUniqueFactorizationDomain(R)/IsUFD, IsIntegralDomain(R)/IsDomain, IsCommutative(R), IsDivisionRing(R), IsUnitary(R), IsFinite(R) (returns cardinality if true).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A true result indicates Magma knows the property holds (even if a stronger property is also true). If no algorithm is available, Magma will give an error. Even if R satisfies a property, certain operations may be unavailable if the category of R does not provide them (e.g., Z7 may be a field mathematically but not a field object in Magma unless explicitly created as one).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subring unitary subtlety
rubrics_metrics.description: A subring is regarded as unitary by Magma only if it contains the multiplicative identity of its parent (generic) ring; having an element acting as a multiplicative identity inside the subring is not sufficient if it's not the parent's 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an ideal I in ZZ/12ZZ may have an element 25 acting as identity within I, but IsUnitary(I) is false if I does not contain the multiplicative identity of ZZ/12ZZ. Be careful when relying on IsUnitary for substructures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations on rings (Characteristic, Centre, UnitGroup, PrimeField/PrimeRing, R+S, R*S, R meet S)
rubrics_metrics.description: General ring-level operations: Characteristic(R), Centre(R), UnitGroup(R), PrimeField(F), PrimeRing(R), and operations combining subrings like R + S (sum), R * S (product), and R meet S (intersection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristic returns smallest m with m*r = 0 for all r or zero. R+S generators are sums of generators; R*S generators are products. Use these operations for ring manipulations and structural queries where algorithms are implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite ring handling (IsFinite, #R, Set(R), iteration)
rubrics_metrics.description: If IsFinite(R) returns true, Magma can usually compute cardinality (#R), enumerate elements (Set(R)), and allow iteration over R (for x in R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use #R for size, Set(R) to obtain the list of elements, and standard iteration constructs when finite. If Magma cannot compute these, IsFinite will be false or an error may result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordered rings operations (comparisons and Max/Min)
rubrics_metrics.description: For totally ordered rings (IsOrdered(R) true, e.g., ZZ, Q, IR), comparison operators (<, ≤, >, ≥) are available, as well as Maximum/Minimum functions over sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparisons where total ordering is defined. Maximum(Q) / Minimum(Q) return both the extremal value and its position in a sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euclidean rings definition and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: A Euclidean ring has a known Euclidean norm φ on its regular elements with properties supporting division-with-remainder; examples include ZZ (φ = absolute value) and univariate polynomials over a field (φ = degree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If IsEuclideanDomain(R) or IsEuclideanRing(R) holds, algorithms relying on Euclidean division (gcds, divisions with remainder) are available. The existence of an implemented Euclidean norm is required for these operations.
